stem: Damini wants to expand $(w+4)(w-4)$ by recognising a conjugate pair.

options.text: $(w+4)(w-4)=w^{2}-16$, because the factors share the same terms with opposite signs.
$(w+4)(w+4)$ is the conjugate pair for this expansion.
The expanded difference $w^{2}-16$ forces the factors $(w+4)$ and $(w-4)$, so start from the difference and skip recognising the pair.
$(w+4)(w-4)=w^{2}+8w-16$, as if both middle terms stay after expansion.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Conjugate factors use the same terms with opposite signs, so the cross-terms cancel and the product is w²−16.

teacher.key_rationale: Conjugates (w+4)(w−4) expand to w²−16 with cross-terms cancelling. Same-sign factors drop the opposite-sign condition. Starting from the difference and skipping the pair reverses recognition. Keeping a middle ±8w uses a different expansion identity.
